title: Array methods
summary: Transform, select, fold and search arrays with map, filter, reduce, find, some, every and includes.

misconceptions.description: Believes map or filter changes the array it is called on instead of returning a new array.
Believes map combines its callback results into one value instead of one result per element.
Believes filter returns the values the callback returned, such as true and false, instead of the elements that passed.
Takes the wrong run of a line that executes many times, counting one run too few or too many.
Reads the value a variable has at the end of the program for every earlier step.
Believes the second argument of reduce is not part of the result.
Believes the starting value of reduce is added again on every pass.
Believes reduce without a starting value starts at 0 and runs the callback for every element.
Believes reduce without a starting value begins with undefined.
Believes find or some return an array of matches, as filter does.
Believes a search method returns null when nothing matches.
Believes some always runs its callback for every element instead of stopping at the first match.

conceptCard.title: map builds a new array
conceptCard.body: map calls a function on every element and collects the returned values in a new array of the same length. The original array is not changed. The function must return a value, or the new array holds undefined.

conceptCard.title: filter keeps what passes
conceptCard.body: filter calls a function on every element and keeps the elements for which it returns a truthy value. The result is a new array that can be shorter, even empty. Its elements are the originals, not the values the function returned.

conceptCard.title: reduce folds to one value
conceptCard.body: reduce folds an array into one value. The callback gets the running result and the current element, and returns the next running result. The second argument is the starting result; without it, the first element is used.

conceptCard.title: Searching an array
conceptCard.body: find returns the first element that passes the test, or undefined. some is true when at least one element passes; every is true only when all pass. includes checks whether an array holds one exact value.
